newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross seeks urgent EU aid for North Korea.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross seeks urgent EU aid for North Korea.

text.p: The European Union's humanitarian office, Echo, has been asked for urgent funds for food aid to flood-hit North Korea, the Geneva-based International Federation of Red Cross (IFRC) said on Wednesday. Jane Grimshaw of the IFRC said she hoped an Echo mission would travel to North Korea later this month to assess the 4.6 million ecu ($3.9 million) request from the British and Danish Red Cross organisations, made in December.
She said the IFRC had no firm date for the mission. "It may take sometime before we get a response," she said.

IFRC representative in North Korea, Ole Gronning of Denmark, on Wednesday predicted a human disaster by the end of the year if relief did not arrive in the communist country where devastating floods in 1995 and 1996 have destroyed rice fields, roads, factories and livestock and swamping mines. On Monday, North Korea admitted that it had only half the grain needed to feed its people. Grimshaw said there were no signs of famine yet but added: "There could be cases of starvation if food is not forthcoming. The situation is alarming."
She said North Korea at present relied totally on Red Cross food supplies.
